title.en: Portfolio positions and asset master data

description.en: How FundsXML describes a portfolio: positions with value, weight and instrument data, the link from each position to its asset in the master data, what happens when the link breaks, and a query for the top holdings in FreeXmlToolkit.

say.en: In this video you read the portfolio of a fund, follow a position to its master data, and list the largest holdings with a query. It takes about four minutes.
The portfolio is part of the fund's dynamic data. It has a NAV date, the valuation day, and a list of positions.

Each position has a UniqueID and identifiers like the ISIN. Then come its currency, its total value in the fund currency, and its weight: eight point three three percent of the net asset value. The last block depends on the kind of instrument. For a share, it holds the number of units and the price.

A bond has a nominal value and a price in percent instead. FundsXML knows many kinds of instruments: shares, bonds, fund shares, warrants, certificates, options, futures, currency forwards, swaps and accounts.

What a security is, is not repeated in every position. The UniqueID points to the asset master data further down. There, asset ID_001 is described once: Apple, a share from the United States, with the LEI of its issuer. If several funds or portfolios hold the same share, its master data still appears only once.

The schema protects this link. Change the UniqueID of the first position to an asset that does not exist, and press F8. The schema reports that there is no asset with this ID, and the data-quality checks add that the position has no master data.
Set the ID back, validate again, and the document is in order.

Now ask the document a question. Press Control K for the Query Console. In the Snippets menu, the FundsXML extension offers ready-made queries. Choose Top 10 positions, load it into the console, and run it.

Click Table to see the result as a list: the ten largest positions, each with the name from the master data, its value and its weight. The query is written in XQuery, so you can adapt it to your own questions.
Thanks for watching. In the next video, you check a FundsXML delivery against the schema and the data-quality rules. The links are on the screen and in the description below.
